ctx.x: Jeunesse Musical du France. Monsieur Levy was the...

Monsieur Levy booked it. Jacob, he was. The impresario. Now the Jeunesse Musical d.u France was an organization just like some of the organizations; it was underwritten by the French government. One of the things about most of those foreign countries, though, Dan, is that they put in money into the arts. Did you know that? Most of them do. And I can't say...well, perhaps they'd do it in America; and then again, maybe I have a right to have this beef, that if they're going to send opera and opera singers to Japan,…

Because jazz is an American thing. It's our black thing. You see? So then why can't...I think I have a legitimate beef. I think that, hell, somebody should phone me and say, "Hey, Sam, what do you think, and what can we do?" And I think that because when you go with an idea you get shut off. They shut you out, Dan. You don't have a chance. You know, I don't have a chance to present anything. I wish I knew what Billy Taylor did, or how he could do it. And I'm calling his name because I have a great respect for him…
